title: Event-driven Admin Step Registry and Support Orchestration CLI
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current runbooks are a mixture of long maintenance docs and ad-hoc scripts. Operators need a composable, event-driven way to execute, inspect, and replay admin flows with clear checkpoints and minimal human error. Existing 'runbooks-as-tasks' efforts are fragmented across repos and shells, making automation brittle and onboarding slow.

Goal: Build a centralized 'Admin Step Registry' (ASR) that models atomic, idempotent admin steps (playbook fragments) as first-class artifacts and exposes them through a small, ergonomic CLI and a lightweight HTTP adapter for automation. Steps will be versioned, annotated with required permissions, and capable of checkpointing state so flows can be resumed or replayed safely. The CLI will provide discoverability, dry-run, argument validation, and automatic audit metadata.

Scope / non-goals: This ticket covers the ASR service model, a developer-facing SDK to register steps, the operator CLI (opsctl-admin), and two example adapters (Slack-trigger and Helix job-trigger). It does NOT include full UI integration into Console or complex RBAC policies beyond role tags and KMS key references (those will follow in a separate ticket).
acceptance_criteria: ASR API deployed to staging with README and example step registration
Operators can list available steps with opsctl-admin --registry <staging> and see description/permissions/version
CLI supports: discover, run --dry-run, run --confirm, resume --checkpoint, and replay --since-timestamp
Each registered step stores: id, semantic version, schema for args, required roles, idempotency token semantics, and optional checkpoint hook
Two adapters implemented: webhook adapter (for Slack/Teams) and Helix-job adapter (for scheduled ops).
All runs emit structured audit events to the ops-event pipeline and are viewable in the staging audit dashboard
Security review completed and KMS integration validated for steps that need secret unwrap
notes: Design decisions: prefer small, composable steps (max ~150 lines of imperative logic) rather than monolithic playbooks to reduce blast radius and enable reuse.
Persistence: use existing ops-config DB (Postgres) for registry metadata and S3 for run logs/checkpoints to allow efficient replay and minimize DB bloat.
Idempotency: each step must accept an idempotency_token and be able to garbage-collect old tokens after 30 days.
API auth: leverage service-to-service mTLS for adapters; operators authenticate via SSO-backed short-lived tokens in the CLI.
Trade-offs: keeping ASR lightweight avoids building a full workflow engine now; orchestration will be achieved by sequencing steps at the caller level or via a later composition layer.
Observability: structured events should include step_id, version, args_hash, run_id, checkpoint_ids, duration_ms, and exit_reason to support post-mortem analysis.
